title: One step of the Game of Life
description:
Conway's Game of Life is played on a grid of cells that are alive (`#`) or dead (`.`). Every cell has up to eight neighbours. In each step:

- a live cell with 2 or 3 live neighbours stays alive, otherwise it dies;
- a dead cell with exactly 3 live neighbours comes alive.

The world is a `std::vector<std::string>`, one string per row. Write:

- `int liveNeighbours(const World& world, int row, int column)`: how many of the (up to eight) surrounding cells are alive. Cells beyond the edge count as dead.
- `World step(const World& world)`: the next generation.

Every cell's fate depends on the **old** world, so build the new world separately rather than changing cells as you go.
hints: For the neighbours, loop `dr` and `dc` over -1, 0 and 1, skip the case where both are 0 (that is the cell itself), and check the position is inside the grid before reading it.
